Lina (PM): Quick sync — we need a compact playbook for customer-requested long pins during migrations. Aim: avoid hard locks on early-stage models.
Omar (Eng): We should support "grant-and-guard": short-duration hard pin (<=90d) + automated guardrails (fallback + throttles) recorded against tenant id.
Jules (Bench): Bench gates proposal: single p95 <= 300ms, quality regression <=1.0% vs baseline, 7d cost soak delta <=30%.
Rina (CS): Customer asked for 120d. Can we offer 90d + migration credit for remaining 30d?
Vik (Sales): Yes — propose 90d hard pin + 30d pro-rated credit tied to observed regressions. Sales can sell the credit as migration insurance.
LegalBot: Note: any >90d hard pin needs legal annex and Security signoff. Draft annex template can include automatic release if rollback triggers happen.
Omar (Eng): Technical points: cache-key must include model_version and tenant_pin_id; runtime must support per-tenant fallback to a vetted variant; implement cost-throttle at runtime (e.g., kick-in at $0.16/1k tokens).
Jules (Bench): Also require daily quality-diff reports and a 48h pre-release soak before granting the hard pin.
Lina (PM): Proposed playbook summary: (1) Grantable hard pin up to 90d with documented SLA annex; (2) optional migration credit up to 60d prorated; (3) gates: p95, quality, cost soak; (4) automated runtime guards (fallback, throttle, per-tenant alerts); (5) legal review for >90d.
Vik (Sales): Action: I'll route the offer to the customer with the 90d+credit option and capture any hard deadlines.
Rina (CS): Action: I'll prepare the migration checklist and KV/cache mapping steps.
Omar (Eng): Action: I'll prototype a tenant-pin flag + fallback route in the next sprint; ETA 2w.
Jules (Bench): Action: will run a 7d cost soak starting today and post results.
Lina (PM): If no objections, I'll formalize the RFC and the catalog policy fields. Approve? :thumbsup: or :eyes:.
Omar (Eng): :thumbsup:.
Jules (Bench): :thumbsup:.
Vik (Sales): :thumbsup:.
LegalBot: :eyes: will post annex draft by EOD.
